LibraryId.description:
A library's opaque token. It says nothing about the library: its kind and
capabilities are fields of its description, and nothing may read them from
here. Sources mint one with [`LibraryId::digest`] over a private key and the
source's identity, so a seen id confirms no guessed location.

ZoteroLibrary.description:
A Zotero library: the personal library ("My Library") or a group by its
Zotero group ID.

oneOf.description:
Read Zotero. `libraries` replaces the chosen libraries (at first the
personal library only); omitted, the current choice is read again.

profile.description:
The Zotero profile to read while Zotero is closed, by the name
`zotero-profiles` gives; never a location. Omitted, a computer with
one profile reads it and one with several is refused.

reload.description: Read everything again, not only what changed.

oneOf.description: The Zotero profiles on this computer, by name; reads no library.

The Zotero group libraries known now, by name: asked of Zotero while
it runs, otherwise those its closed copy listed when last read.

ErrorReason.description:
Why a request failed, when the code alone cannot tell a caller what to change.
Front ends choose their words from it; they never guess a reason from the code.

oneOf.description: No style has the requested id; `styles` lists them.
No output has the requested id; `outputs` lists them.
The requested locale is not bundled; `styles` lists the locales.
The key is repeated in a library, so every entry under it is skipped.
Several references share the key.
A key output needs a citation key this reference does not have.
The program started as the Ibis app does not exist.
The program started as the Ibis app is not Ibis.
The Ibis app started but did not confirm the request in time.
Zotero is running but does not let other applications read it.
Zotero is closed and which profile to read is not settled; name one.
A closed read is unsafe or impossible here; opening Zotero is the fix.
No Zotero library is on this computer.
A closed read needs a private copy and there is no room for it.
A CSV file's first row does not name the columns of Ibis's template.

refresh_reason.description: What a person can do about `refresh_error`, when the failure says.

watch_warning.description: A readable source remains usable when automatic updates are unavailable.

zotero.description: Which Zotero library this is, for a Zotero library.

LibraryKind.description: What a library is. Front ends read this, never the library's id.

oneOf.description: A BibTeX, BibLaTeX, CSL-JSON, RIS or CSV file.
Data handed to the engine whole, with no source behind it.

SourceCapability.description:
A fixed list per kind, not a plugin system. Zotero's two read paths share
one kind, so running and closed Zotero cannot offer different lists.

key.description:
The repeated citation key or CSL `id`, for `duplicate-key` only. It is the person's
own data and is shown only to them; no other warning carries source text.

WarningCode.description: Safe source diagnostics contain a location and fixed code, never payloads.

oneOf.description:
Better BibTeX keeps keys this read could not get, so items without a
key of their own have none rather than a guessed one.

ZoteroGroup.description: A Zotero group library by its public ID and a name safe to show.

ZoteroLibrary.description:
A Zotero library: the personal library ("My Library") or a group by its
Zotero group ID.

zotero_installed.description: Answers `zotero-profiles`: whether a Zotero library is on this computer.

zotero_profiles.description: Answers `zotero-profiles`: each profile's safe name, never its location.

interpret_locator.description:
Read a locator typed at the end of the query (`smith p 45`) and search
for the rest; the result says what was read so it can be undone.

libraries.description: Omitted searches every loaded library; an empty list searches none.

page_index.description: Zero-based physical index, distinct from the printed page label.

parent.description: The attachment, not an invented bibliographic parent.

content_hash.description: Identifies the file contents without exposing a path or attachment URL.

CitationWarningCode.description: Fixed codes only; source diagnostics never include field text or locations.

Identifier.description: A recognized identifier in canonical form.

oneOf.description: An ISBN, PubMed ID or arXiv ID given as the whole query.

text.description: Untrusted plain text; front ends must never inject this as HTML.

added_at.description: Source-added metadata; affects recents/display, never citation meaning.

csl.description: Normalised CSL data; all variables may affect a chosen style.

identifiers.description:
Search-only identifiers (for example arXiv eprints), never invented as
printed CSL fields. They invalidate display/search, not citation picks.

warnings.description: Item-local conversion uncertainty, independent of CSL and source paths.

conditions.description: Source conditions are data only; this contract never executes them.

partial.description:
Some terms did not match: one of the closest matches, given only when
nothing matches every term.

typo.description: Some term matched only with one typo.

TrailingLocator.description: A search with a locator split off its end.

typed.description: The text read as the locator, exactly as typed.

locator.description: The locator read off the end of the query, when one was asked for and found.

command.description: A command name for syntaxes that support it; engines validate its grammar.

oneOf.description:
An output by its id in the engine's `outputs` list: a key syntax or a
common style. The engine writes it as that entry's own output.

TextRun.description: Fixed-depth rich text: styling is data, never arbitrary HTML or executable markup.

input_language.description: None uses en-US, never the process or operating-system locale.

items.description: Input order and duplicate references are meaningful and must be preserved.

output_locale.description: None uses the style default. Engines validate locale strings as data.

AppId.description:
An app as the platform names it: a bundle ID on macOS, an executable name
on Windows. Never a window title or document name.

CitationError.description:
Fixed citation diagnostics contain no source data, paths, keys or request text.
A front-end boundary maps a wholly invalid/cancelled request to its envelope error.

CitationWarningCode.description: Fixed codes only; source diagnostics never include field text or locations.

CopyReason.description: Why a citation was copied instead of pasted.

oneOf.description: An unrecognised app has no explicit paste approval.
System-wide secure typing is enabled, possibly by another app.
The final paste check was unavailable or could not finish in time.
macOS Accessibility trust is required for the identity-only focus proof.
A paste would replace selected text the search never showed.
A changed citation replaces only the old citation, selected.

Destination.description:
What Ibis does for a named app: the output it uses and whether it pastes,
with pasting on and permitted, as they are by default. A choice remembered
in the app for one app is that person's and stays out of this answer.

name.description: The app's name, when Ibis knows it.

output_question.description: The app keeps `output` until a person answers this question in Ibis.

DisplayNode.description: One display group owns ordered text leaves; shared punctuation has no item.

DisplayRun.description:
Output-only passive presentation. The smaller request TextRun contract stays
independent of the additional styles a citation processor may produce.

DisplayTree.description: A bounded-depth tree: root -> ownership groups -> styled text leaves.

item.description: Zero-based request index; None describes a request-wide loss.

OutputQuestion.description: An app ID that cannot tell Ibis which output its document needs.

command.description: A command name for syntaxes that support it; engines validate its grammar.

oneOf.description:
An output by its id in the engine's `outputs` list: a key syntax or a
common style. The engine writes it as that entry's own output.

System.description: The operating system an app ID belongs to.

content_hash.description: Digest of the exact clipboard representations, including their presence.

destination.description: The app this citation was made for, when a caller named one.

language.description:
The language a formatted citation is written in, whatever the interface
uses. Key syntaxes have none: the destination's processor decides.

outcomes.description: Exactly one outcome per request item, addressed by its zero-based index.

params.description:
Exact keys to look for in one project `.bib`, which stays out of the search
libraries. Reading it never writes to it.
params.title: ProjectRequest

Doubt.description: Why a key that is written in the file may not be the intended reference.

oneOf.description: The entry and the library disagree on DOI, title or year.
A key differs only by letter case; BibTeX treats them as one.
The key is written as another entry's `ids` alias.
The key belongs to an `@xdata` entry, which cannot be cited.
The key is inside `@comment`. Biber skips it; classic BibTeX reads it.

KeyCheck.description: One emitted key against one bibliography.

oneOf.description: Only after a complete scan.

ProjectKey.description: One key against the chosen file.

ProjectProblem.description: Why a read could not be used.

oneOf.description: Missing, online-only or not reachable in time.
A project bibliography is BibTeX or BibLaTeX.

damaged_lines.description: Lines that could not be read, which is why nothing can be called missing.

name.description: The file's name, never its folder.

problem.description: Why this read could not be used; the answers then say "could not check".

params.description: One reference's original BibTeX entry, with what it needs to stand alone.
params.title: EntryRequest

EntryRefusal.description: Why an entry's original text cannot be copied, so a person can re-export it.

oneOf.description: The reference does not come from a BibTeX file, so no original exists.
The file changed since the library was read, or could not be read.
It relies on a `crossref`, `xdata` or `@string` that cannot come with it.
The entry as written, with the `@string`, `crossref` and `xdata` it needs.

params.description: A page of the style list: the curated styles first, then the rest by id.

query.description: Words from a style's title or id; every word must match.

params.title: StylesRequest

curated.description: One of the styles offered first.

default_locale.description: The language this style is written in unless a request names another.

format.description: CSL's citation format, such as `author-date`, `numeric` or `note`.

parent.description: The independent style whose rules this one uses.

updated.description: The style's own last-changed date: its only version marker.

locales.description: Every language a style can be written in.

styles_release.description: Styles change only with an Ibis release; these say which release.

total.description: How many styles match the request, beyond this page.

OutputInfo.description: One output, as the `outputs` method lists it.

description.description:
A style's full title, shown only as the quiet detail beside the name;
none when it is the name.

entries.description:
It writes reference entries, never in-text citations: a numbered
style cannot number one citation alone.

example.description:
What it writes for one invented reference: the key `key`, or for a
style an article by A. García (2021).

exports_records.description:
It writes each reference's whole record, notes included, not a
citation; agents are not offered it.

forms.description: The forms one reference can be cited in.

id.description:
Stable: settings store it, `--format` and MCP's `format` take it, and
`{"kind":"preset","name":ID}` names it in a request.

name.description: The one name every front end shows, short enough for "APA · Word".

output.description: The output a request names for it.

command.description: A command name for syntaxes that support it; engines validate its grammar.

oneOf.description:
An output by its id in the engine's `outputs` list: a key syntax or a
common style. The engine writes it as that entry's own output.

default.description: The id used when nothing names an output.

default_style.description: The id of the style used when finished text is wanted and nothing names a style.

outputs.description: The key outputs first, then the common styles, most used first.
